learning: Iteration 8 showed the slalom is stuck at its max_error floor (0.065) with 1.1 line losses and low oscillation (0.20), so it is reacting late rather than jittering. Geometry has no lever left on it. Speed is the next controller lever to test, since the oval has ample time margin.
notes: Iteration 9 package: iteration 8 geometry held unchanged, with base_speed reduced from 1.5 to 1.3 as the only change. Aimed at the slalom, which loses the line on alternating bends at low oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 8 (score 667.95) is the best measured design: body_length 0.10, mass 0.6, sensors at y 0.075, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.09. The oval finished 20 of 20 with max_error 0.0165 and oscillation 0.21. The s-bend finished 19 of 20 with line losses 0.8 and oscillation 0.32, which is under the 0.35 limit. The slalom has 0 finishes, progress 0.34, 1.1 line losses per run and max_error at the 0.065 floor, while its oscillation is low at 0.20. Low oscillation with high line loss means the robot is late on alternating bends, not jittering. Iterations 5 to 7 showed the slalom ignores yaw inertia, and iteration 4 showed a larger footprint trades oval reliability for slalom retention. Geometry therefore stays at the iteration 8 values, so the only variable is the controller. I lower base_speed from 1.5 to 1.3. Less forward speed gives the steering loop more time to correct on the alternating slalom bends, and the signal is unchanged. Oval time was 1.72 s at 1.5, so at 1.3 it should be about 2.0 s, well inside the 3 s limit. Gains kp 2.8, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, weights and last_direction are unchanged. Expected, not measured: slalom progress above 0.34 and line losses at or below 1.1, with the s-bend still at 19 or more finishes and the oval still at 20 of 20. Risk: if the s-bend falls below 19 finishes, the speed cut is costing time on the bends, so the next step should return to 1.5 and test kd.
